disease_label_per_paper: Disseminated gonococcal infection presenting with pustular rash and hand tenosynovitis
presentation_summary: 23-year-old sexually active woman presented with left wrist pain and two small pustular lesions on the left palm and thenar eminence.
She denied drainage from pustules and fever; initial vitals were HR 126/min, temperature 99.1 F, RR 18/min, and BP 130/76 mmHg.
Left wrist was tender with limited hand movement especially on extension; WBC was 24,900/uL and hand/wrist x-ray was normal.

She was initially discharged on Augmentin for presumed staphylococcal infection, but pain worsened and CT later showed tenosynovitis in the fourth extensor compartment without abscess or septic arthritis.

Wound culture from a pustular lesion grew Neisseria gonorrhoeae; urine gonococcus testing was negative, chlamydia testing was positive, blood cultures were negative, and ESR/CRP were within normal limits.

clinical_course: Symptoms worsened after initial discharge on Augmentin.
Edema and range-of-motion limitation persisted despite active antibiotics.
Radical tenosynovectomy led to resolution of symptoms.
Discharged home on IV ceftriaxone with infectious disease follow-up.
quality_warnings: The gonococcal wound culture and urine STI tests are retained as non-ranking confirmatory evidence.
The case intentionally preserves normal ESR/CRP and negative blood culture because DGI can be culture-negative outside lesion or mucosal sites.
